text: Section 37.1 asks whether spacetime's emergence from a non-spatiotemporal substrate is strong or weak. What is the working assumption of the theoretical-physics community, and on what grounds?
choices: Strong emergence, because spacetime is ontologically additional to the substrate, just as Chalmers argues consciousness is
Weak emergence, because spatiotemporal structure is taken to be in-principle derivable from the substrate, as temperature and pressure are from microphysics
Neither, because dualities like AdS/CFT are merely notational, on a par with expressing temperature in Celsius versus Fahrenheit
Strong emergence, because the Ryu-Takayanagi relation cannot in principle be derived from the boundary theory
explanation: The standard assumption is weak emergence: like temperature or pressure, spacetime is held to be in-principle derivable from the substrate, with AdS/CFT and the Ryu-Takayanagi formula as the worked examples. Strong emergence (ontologically additional, in-principle underivable) is Chalmers's claim about consciousness and is explicitly not the working hypothesis; Huggett and Wuthrich also argue the duality is substantive, not mere notation.
